analysis.title: Learn to love VIX 30
key_insights: VIX recorded its fifth-largest weekly spike in history, behind the GFC, COVID, the Flash Crash and Liberation Day.
Panic extends beyond equities. Marlin cites a record 2-week change in the all-in-barrel oil price, bigger than GFC and COVID.
Gold options showed extreme stress. On November 20th, 3-month normalized 25 delta put-call skew and implied vol moved 4-5 standard deviations, with skew at a multiyear max (per Steno).
Bitcoin ATM implied vol spiked across expiries (per GS vol desk).
FX and bond 3-month ATM vol percentiles are calm relative to equities, oil and gold (per Marquee).
Liquidity is thin. S&P futures top-of-book depth averaged $4.2 million on Thursday, among the weakest readings in four years (per GS trading desk).
Historically, VIX above 30 has been followed by better forward S&P 500 returns than VIX 20-30, and above 35 average subsequent 12-month returns exceeded 20% (per Jefferies).
Goldman's US Vol Panic Index is at 9.2 out of 10, and readings above 9.5 have historically signaled near-term relief.
VIX is in the highest 5% of observations since 1990, and buying at such fear levels has historically delivered stronger long-term returns, though panic can deepen (per GBM and Bilello).
